newsitem.title: UK: British bank shares taking stock after election.
newsitem.headline: British bank shares taking stock after election.

text.p: British bank shares were underperformimg amid market uncertainty after the election, particularly about interest rates, dealers said on Friday.
Barclays Plc shares were down 5.5 pence, or 0.48 percent, to 1,142.5p by 0915 GMT in volume of 570,000 while National Westminster Bank Plc was off 4.5p at 722.5p (630,000).
The FTSE-100 index was 6.3 points, or 0.14 percent, lower at 4438.7.
"The sector had a pre-emptive markdown first thing and bargain hunters have been bringing it back up," a marketmaker at a British bank said.
Barclays was 16p lower at one stage while NatWest was off 10p. Lloyds TSB Group Plc was down 5p at 553.5p after an earlier 543p low.
Dealers said volume was low in the British equity market generally and likely to remain so until after Labour's finance minister, likely to be Gordon Brown, made a statement.
Britain's Labour Party won a landslide victory in Thursday's election, ousting the Conservative Party from power after 18 years in office.
The monthly U.S. jobs report, due at 1230 GMT, was also capping activity, dealers said.
